messages.subject: Bootstrapping
parts:
Hi
The following two models don't seem to work for me when I try to perform the bootstrapping on them -  it normally takes about 20 minutes or so to bootstrap my models but I have waited over an hour for this to work and it doesn't. Is this because one of the constructs (PF3) has only 2 observed variables? How do I get around this?

> SCTModel14 <- '
+ PF3=~pers5+pers2 
+ Control=~ Env15+Env14+Env13
+ BehF1=~BF7_AV+BF6_AV+BF4_AV+BF3_AV+BF2_AV+BF1_AV
+ 
+ # direct effect
+ BehF1~ c*PF3
+ # mediator
+ Control ~ a*PF3
+ BehF1 ~ b*Control
+ # indirect effect (a*b)
+ indirect := a*b
+ # total effect
+ total := c + (a*b)
+ '
> SCT1fit14<-sem(SCTModel14, data = SMBI_Alldata, test = "bollen.stine",  se="boot", bootstrap = 5000)



SCTModel15 <- '

PF3=~pers5+pers2

Control=~ Env15+Env14+Env13

BehF2=~BF9_AV+BF10_AV+BF11_AV+BF12_AV

 

 

# direct effect

             BehF2~ c*PF3

           # mediator

            Control ~ a*PF3

             BehF2 ~ b*Control

           # indirect effect (a*b)

             indirect := a*b

           # total effect

             total := c + (a*b)

         '

 

SCT1fit15<-sem(SCTModel15, data = SMBI_Alldata, test = "bollen.stine",  se="boot", bootstrap = 5000)

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Bootstrapping
parts: Is this because one of the constructs (PF3) has only 2 observed variables?

Hard to tell without knowing anything about your data.  The model is globally identified because PF3 is related to other variables, but you can certainly try fixing both factor loadings to 1 (in which case the factor variance represents the covariance between the two indicators, which I find intuitively appealing).
How do I get around this?

Well, you requested 5000 bootstrap samples, which is a lot.  Parallel computing can reduce the time by half if you use 3 cores (most computers have 4 available nowadays, or 8 if you have a good one).  Instead of requesting bootstraps in the lavaan call, just run your model with appropriate defaults.

SCT1fit14 <- sem(SCTModel14, data = SMBI_Alldata)

Then bootstrap afterward.  The advantage is you can start with 100 bootstrap samples to see how long it takes, then estimate how long 5000 would take.  Also, this way you can request parallel computing.

library(parallel)
## Bollen-Stine bootstrap p value
bootstrapLRT(SCT1fit14, R = 100, parallel = "snow", ncpus = detectCores() - 1)
## if you have a Mac, request parallel = "multicore"

## bootstrap coefficients
bCoefs <- bootstrapLavaan(SCT1fit14, R = 100, parallel = "snow", ncpus = detectCores() - 1)
## get percentile CIs
apply(bCoefs, 2, quantile, probs = c(.025, .975))
